title: Poisson regression as a named count GLM
dek: Wikipedia Poisson regression: log λ = xᵀβ. Offsets, overdispersion, and quasi-Poisson already have Simplfy plates.
story: Poisson regression on Wikipedia is the count celebrity: Y ~ Poisson(λ), log λ = xᵀβ, sometimes with offset log(exposure). It is a GLM, not a separate software button.
stats-poisson already owns the likelihood. stats-overdispersion already says mean=variance is a marriage you may not have. This card is the encyclopedia name.
TB colony counts, read depths, and incident-case tallies are the usual lab objects — still not a reason to ignore extra-Poisson variance.
deepTitle: Offset, exposure, and the cousin models
deep: Offset is a coefficient frozen at 1, not a forgotten covariate.
Negative binomial is a different random component (wiki-negbin).
Quasi-Poisson keeps V(μ)=φμ without a full NB likelihood.
Zero-inflation is yet another model, not a Poisson with a Wikipedia footnote.

visual.caption: Teaching bars: Poisson marriage (mean=var) versus overdispersed counts. Not a simulation study.
